firstDiff: I joined a queer pungmul (풍물) ensemble because I wanted to learn traditional Korean music and find people with whom I could play it. I love the force of the drums and gongs and the way a performance develops as everyone listens and responds to one another. Learning more about the music has also introduced me to histories beyond our group, from communal gatherings to performances associated with South Korea's democracy movement. I am grateful to have a small place in this living tradition.

-

Our ensemble gave a formal concert in 2024, and we participate in the Seoul Pride parade every year. We also busk seasonally and perform at smaller events supporting queer rights. Through these performances, I have found a way to share a Korean cultural tradition with people among whom I feel at home. In a country where 2SLGBTQ+ rights remain contested, playing in public carries a significance beyond the music. I am glad that we can be heard there, together.
